input:
A curve passes through the point (1, π/6). Let the slope of the curve at each point (x, y) be y/x + sec(y/x), x > 0, then, the equation of the curve is

Options:
A. sin(y/x) = log(x) + 1/2
B. cosec(y/x) = log(x) + 2
C. sec(2y/x) = log(x) + 2
D. cos(2y/x) = log(x) + 1/2

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Solve the homogeneous differential equation dy/dx = y/x + sec(y/x) passing through (1, π/6).
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: This is a homogeneous DE in y/x. Substitute y = vx, then dy/dx = v + x(dv/dx). The v terms cancel, leading to a simple separable DE.

key_concepts: Homogeneous differential equation substitution: y = vx
Separation of variables: cos v dv = (1/x) dx
Integrating factor/standard integrals: ∫ cos v dv = sin v

key_formulas.substitution: v + x dv/dx = v + sec v
key_formulas.separated: 1/sec v dv = 1/x dx  ⇒  cos v dv = (1/x) dx
key_formulas.general_solution: sin v = log x + c  ⇒  sin(y/x) = log x + c

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute y = vx, simplify to cos v dv = (1/x) dx, integrate to find sin(y/x) = log x + c, and use point (1, π/6) to find c.
logical_steps: Step 1: Put y = vx ⇒ dy/dx = v + x dv/dx
Step 2: Equate v + x dv/dx = v + sec v
Step 3: Cancel v: x dv/dx = sec v ⇒ cos v dv = (1/x) dx
Step 4: Integrate: sin v = log x + c ⇒ sin(y/x) = log x + c
Step 5: Substitute (1, π/6): sin(π/6) = log 1 + c ⇒ 1/2 = 0 + c ⇒ c = 1/2
Step 6: Write solution sin(y/x) = log x + 1/2 and match option

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: At x=1, y=π/6: sin(π/6) = 1/2, log(1) + 1/2 = 1/2 ✓. Differentiating sin(y/x) = log x + 1/2: cos(y/x)·(x dy/dx - y)/x² = 1/x ⇒ x dy/dx - y = x/cos(y/x) = x sec(y/x) ⇒ dy/dx = y/x + sec(y/x) ✓
